title: cross-region autoscale feedback loop caused duplicated assignments and misroute avalanche
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: On 2026-03-09 a cross-region autoscaling event interacted with the routing control plane’s drain/TTL signals causing duplicated assignment records and a widespread misroute/fallback cascade. The incident increased P50 latency by ~3x for affected tenants, triggered large-scale fallback to smaller model variants, and spiked token costs for a 20-minute window.
impact_details: Approximately 14% of production requests across EU and US regions experienced increased latency and partial responses. Some customers saw degraded quality due to fallbacks to low-capacity model variants. No customer data was leaked; no security controls were violated. The incident lasted ~22 minutes from first misroute spike to rollback stabilization.
timeline: 2026-03-09 09:04 UTC: Scheduled autoscaling action triggered in eu-central after a transient capacity pressure signal.
2026-03-09 09:05 UTC: Regional autoscaler emitted a soft-decommission (soft-drain) with a short TTL while new nodes were provisioning.

2026-03-09 09:06 UTC: Control plane aggregator applied the soft-drain and, due to a TTL collision bug, converted the state to a persistent tombstone. Duplicate assignment records for several routing shards were written.

2026-03-09 09:07 UTC: Router replicas reading the shard assignments detected conflicting ownership; some replicas interpreted the persistent tombstone as permanent unavailability and routed traffic to lower-tier model variants and secondary regions.

2026-03-09 09:09 UTC: Fallback policy executed at scale as multiple regions simultaneously reported apparent capacity loss. This caused a spike in requests to the shared fallback model pool, increasing token costs and load on fallback nodes.
2026-03-09 09:12 UTC: Observability alerts (routing-oscillation and fallback-rate) fired; on-call began investigation.
2026-03-09 09:18 UTC: Team applied emergency mitigation: temporary hold on autoscaler-induced soft-drains and forced reconciliation of assignment state from the control plane master snapshot.
2026-03-09 09:26 UTC: Traffic returned to expected variants and regions; follow-up rolling patch to routing aggregator deployed 2026-03-09 11:02 UTC to prevent TTL conversion bug.
2026-03-09 11:30 UTC: Post-incident monitoring window closed after 24h without recurrence.
2026-03-10 10:00 UTC: Drafted postmortem and routed to PM/Design/Infra for review.
2026-03-14 14:20 UTC: Final postmortem approved and action items assigned.
root_cause: A TTL collision bug in the routing control plane's drain aggregator incorrectly escalated short-lived soft-drain signals from the autoscaler into persistent tombstones. These tombstones produced duplicated assignment entries across shard replicas; inconsistent reads led routers to believe nodes were permanently unavailable and to trigger fallbacks simultaneously across regions. The control plane lacked adequate hysteresis between soft-decommissions and hard decommissions under concurrent autoscale events.
mitigations_applied: Immediate: disabled autoscaler-induced soft-drains for affected regions to stop new tombstones being generated.
Immediate: forced control plane reconciliation using latest master snapshot to clear duplicate assignment records.
Short-term: throttled fallback policy to add rate-limit windows and backoff to avoid amplifying downstream load.
Long-term: deployed patch to the drain aggregator to preserve soft-drain TTL semantics and avoid automatic tombstone promotion (runtime-1.20).
action_items: ENG-89766: Add unit + integration tests covering TTL overlap scenarios in drain aggregator (owner: Liang Zhou, due: 2026-03-31).
ENG-89767: Implement control-plane reconciliation job that detects duplicate assignments and triggers idempotent cleanup (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2026-04-07).
ENG-89768: Add observability metric 'soft_drain_promotion_rate' and dashboard tile; correlate with autoscaler events (owner: Marco Hernández, due: 2026-03-24).
ENG-89769: Harden fallback policy with exponential backoff and token budget caps to prevent cost amplification during multi-region events (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2026-04-14).
ENG-89770: Update runbook for on-call to include autoscaler -> drain interaction checklist and emergency mitigations (owner: Aisha Patel, due: 2026-03-21).
postmortem_notes: Root cause required cross-team collaboration between autoscaler, control plane, and router teams; decision path: preserve soft-drain TTL semantics and add reconciliation instead of increasing autoscaler delay.
PM/Design feedback: surface 'degraded-variant' feedback in Console so customers see what variant they were routed to during incidents.
Operations feedback: recovery time could be shortened by exposing reconciliation tools to on-call with scoped permissions.
We considered adding a manual autoscaler hold for high-impact customers; decided to build automated safe-holds tied to SLAs instead (follow-up PR planned).

resolution: Patched the drain aggregator to stop promoting soft-drains to tombstones, added a reconciliation job, throttled fallback policy, and updated runbook. Released fixes in runtime-1.20 and deployed fallback throttles behind a gradual rollout flag. No recurrence observed in 7-day monitoring window.
lessons_learned: Soft signals (soft-drain) must be treated with stronger hysteresis in a distributed control plane; TTL collisions are a real failure mode under concurrent autoscale events.
Fallback policies need explicit amplification controls (rate limits and token budgets) to avoid cost spikes when many routers decide to fallback at once.
On-call tooling should include a safe reconciliation path that non-core teams can trigger with guardrails to shorten MTTR.
Cross-team tabletop drills that simulate autoscaler + routing interactions will help catch these multi-component failure modes earlier.
